rows.name: level_timer_TIME (3-digit BCD countdown)
rows.notes: World 1-1 TIME countdown. Encoding: 3 BCD digits, 0x07F8 hundreds, 0x07F9 tens, 0x07FA ones; the HUD redraws each decrement. Found with no reference by differential search: standing still in 1-1, two wait-rounds with filter 'decreased' left 23 then 10 survivors; 0x07F9 and 0x07FA were among them and a direct read of 0x07F8-0x07FA gave [3,3,6] matching a displayed TIME. Proof by write_memory + screenshot: while paused, write_memory 0x07F8-0x07FA = [1,2,3] then step_frame 1 redrew TIME to 119 (the timer ticks ~4 counts per stepped frame in this emulator); a second write of [5,5,5] then step_frame 1 showed TIME 551, exactly the three bytes [5,5,1]. Screenshot: the top-right TIME field read the written value.

rows.name: coin_count (two decimal digits: tens 0x07ED, ones 0x07EE)
rows.notes: World 1-1 HUD coin counter next to the coin icon ("x NN"). Encoding: TWO decimal digit bytes, tens at 0x07ED and ones at 0x07EE, displayed verbatim (the HUD copies each byte straight into a digit tile, so a non-digit value shows as a letter). Found with no reference by differential search: the first ? block in 1-1 (level x=256, hit from below) gives one coin and +200 points; a snapshot pair around that grab (filter 'increased') and a direct read showed 0x07EE 0->1 while 0x07ED stayed 0. Proof by write_memory + screenshot (the coin HUD redraws only when the game changes the count, so the deterministic grab was replayed): (a) write_memory 0x07EE = 7 then grab the coin -> HUD showed x08; (b) write_memory 0x07ED = 9, 0x07EE = 0x10 then force a time-up death (which redraws the status bar) -> HUD showed the tens tile '9' and the ones tile 0x10 rendered as a letter, proving the two bytes are copied directly; (c) write_memory 0x07ED = 0, 0x07EE = 9 then grab the coin -> 0x07ED=1, 0x07EE=0 and the HUD showed x10 (carry proven). This 'World' ROM keeps the coin count as a digit pair, unlike the single-byte layout sometimes assumed.

rows.name: score (6 decimal digits, most significant first)
rows.notes: World 1-1 HUD score under MARIO (six digits). Encoding: six decimal digit bytes at 0x07DD-0x07E2, most significant at 0x07DD, tens at 0x07E2; the ones digit is always 0 and is not stored (0x07E3 is not part of the value and the HUD appends a fixed 0). Found with no reference by differential search: the coin grab (+200) raised the displayed score from 000000 to 000200 and, on a snapshot pair, changed 0x07E1 (the hundreds digit) by +2. Proof by write_memory + screenshot (the status bar redraws only on an event, so a time-up death was used): write_memory 0x07DC..0x07E3 = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8], then set the timer to 0 to force a time-up death; the redrawn HUD showed 2345670 - i.e. only 0x07DD(2), 0x07DE(3), 0x07DF(4), 0x07E0(5), 0x07E1(6), 0x07E2(7) appeared, while the out-of-range 0x07DC(1) and 0x07E3(8) did not. A separate write of 0x07DD-0x07E2 = [0,0,9,9,9,0] reproduced 099900 on the next redraw. 0x07D7-0x07DC is the separate TOP score display and is not the current score.
